# Research Verdict

**
Bottom Line:** Yes, for pristine, localized microscale regions of natural-abundance cubic boron arsenide (c-BAs
), room-temperature thermal conductivity ($\kappa$) reaches ~1200–1300 W/mK
[3, 10], reconciling with four-phonon *ab initio* predictions of ~1400 W/mK [2
]. However, ~1300 W/mK is neither the bulk engineering average nor the absolute ceiling: point defects
and impurities routinely depress millimeter-scale bulk regions below 1000 W/mK [7, 12], while isotop

ically enriched crystals have recently reached ~1500 W/mK [4].

## theory predictions
First
-principles three-phonon calculations by Lindsay, Broido, and Reinecke (2013) initially predicted room-temperature $\kappa$ exceeding
2000 W/mK for c-BAs [1]. Incorporating four-phonon scattering (Feng et al., 201
7) reduced the predicted room-temperature value from 2200 W/mK to 1400

W/mK [2].

## experimental measurements
In 2018, Kang et al. measured
1300 W/mK in defect-free c-BAs regions via time-domain thermoreflectance (
TDTR) [3], while Li et al. and Tian et al. independently reported $1000 \pm
In 2022, optical transient grating measurements confirmed $\kappa \approx 1200$ W/mK alongside high amb
ipolar mobility (1600 $\text{cm}^2/\text{V}\cdot\text{s}$) at the same sample
locations [10], and subsequent syntheses of isotopically enriched c-BAs reached $\approx 1500$

W/mK [4].

## method disputes
Secondary ion mass spectrometry and electron probe microanalysis confirm that Si
, C, O, and other impurities substantially degrade bulk thermal conductivity in chemical vapor transport (CVT) crystals [7]. In
TDTR measurements, ballistic phonon transport at small heater spot sizes systematically depresses apparent measured $\kappa$ below the intrinsic bulk value rather than inflating

it [8, 9].

## applications and outlook
While CVT growth suffers from size scalability and quality control limitations that
prevent wafer-scale deployment [11], individual crystals have exceeded the 2 mm threshold (reaching $4\text{ mm} \times
2\text{ mm} \times 1\text{ mm}$ at ~900 W/m
K) [12]. Furthermore, although c-BAs exhibits a room-temperature thermal expansion coefficient ($3.85 \times 1
0^{-6}\text{ K}^{-1}$) well matched to GaN [13], practical heterointegration remains constrained
by interfacial thermal resistance across required buffer layers such as $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ [1

4].

## Contested & ruled
No formal human adjudication was required. On `c8`, the strict <
2 mm ceiling is contested because 4 mm crystals were reported [12], though commercial wafer-scale integration remains unachieved

[11].
